mission.title: YOUR MISSION
mission.text: Your mission today is to draft a 225-word formal description of someone you admire. You must use specific writing techniques to prove your points.

stages.name: Lead-in
stages.aim: To engage students and activate schema regarding 'admirable' figures.

slides.title: Who is a hero?
slides.question: Brainstorm two adjectives for each person.
slides.notes: Teacher Scaffolding: Elicit adjectives to board. Ask CCQs about why these specific figures are admired.

stages.name: Preparation
stages.aim: To brainstorm and plan the content of the description.

slides.title: How to build a profile
slides.text: Before you start, look at this example:

points.text: Supporting Fact: She trained for [HIGHLIGHT: 5,300 hours] before her debut.

slides.notes: Pedagogy: Model how to connect an abstract trait (Hard-working) to a concrete, provable fact (5,300 hours).

slides.title: The Admirable Profile
slides.content:
StepInstruction
1Choose your person.
2List 3 admirable traits.
3Provide 1 supporting fact for each trait.
slides.notes: Circulate and assist students in finding specific facts for their subjects.

stages.name: Preparation
stages.aim: To introduce the 'Supporting your opinion' strategy and 'Attitude Adverbs' focus.

slides.context_sentence: Amazingly, she won the gold medal despite her injury.
Remarkably, he survived the crash without any scratches.
Generously, they decided to donate all their money to charity.
Fortunately, he found his missing passport just before the flight.
Clearly, the team managed to win the game in the final minute.

slides.title: Supporting Your Opinion
slides.main_text: When you express an opinion, [HIGHLIGHT: give real-life examples and facts to support it].
slides.notes: Compare 'Messi is good' vs 'Messi has won 8 Ballon d'Ors.' Which proves greatness?

stages.name: Task
stages.aim: To produce the 225-word first draft using the models and language from Stages 2-3.

slides.title: First Draft (225 words)
slides.content:
PointChecklist
OpinionState your opinion clearly
AdverbsUse attitude adverbs correctly
FactsSupport every point with a fact
slides.notes: Assist with active use of adverbs. Help with relative clauses.

slides.title: Read your closing statement to a partner.

task_2_sentences: She won the gold medal despite her injury.
He survived the crash without any scratches.
They decided to donate all their money to charity.
He found his missing passport just before the flight.
The team managed to win the game in the final minute.
She has written ten books by the age of twenty.
